description: Network Protocols are a standard set of rules that govern data communication between devices in a computer network. The functioning of the internet primarily relies on the TCP/IP suite and other application-level protocols.

sections.title: Basics of Protocols
sections.description: Fundamental technical concepts required to understand how network communication operates.

key_concepts.explanation: A standard set of rules and guidelines that determine how data is formatted, transmitted, and received across a network.
A 16-bit logical address that identifies a specific process, application, or network service. The total number of available ports is 65,535.
The method of dividing digital data into smaller blocks, called packets, so they can be transmitted efficiently and routed independently over a network.

sections.title: Core Communication Protocols
sections.description: The primary transmission and routing protocols that form the absolute foundation of the Internet.

key_concepts.explanation: It is a connection-oriented protocol that ensures the safe, error-free, and ordered delivery of data packets across a network.
It is the primary network layer protocol that uses IP addresses to route and deliver data packets from the source to their final destination.
A connectionless protocol that is significantly faster than TCP but does not guarantee the delivery or ordering of data. It is primarily used in video streaming and online multiplayer gaming.

sections.title: Web and File Transfer Protocols
sections.description: Major application-layer protocols specifically used for web browsing and transferring files over the internet.

key_associations.extra_info: The foundation of the World Wide Web (WWW). It transmits hypertext and web pages between a web browser (client) and a web server.
It is the secure and encrypted version of HTTP that utilizes SSL/TLS protocols to protect data integrity and privacy.
A standard network protocol used for the transfer of computer files (downloading and uploading) between a client and server on a computer network.

sections.title: Email Protocols
sections.description: Standard protocols utilized for sending, receiving, and managing electronic mail across networks.

key_associations.extra_info: It is a push protocol strictly used for sending email messages from a client to a mail server or between mail servers.
It is a pull protocol used to download emails from the server to the local device. It usually deletes the original copy from the server after downloading.
It is an advanced alternative to POP3. It allows multiple users to read, organize, and manage emails directly on the mail server without downloading them.

sections.title: Important Facts and Other Protocols
sections.description: Crucial one-liner facts and auxiliary network protocols important from an examination perspective.

important_facts.fact: DNS (Domain Name System) translates human-readable Domain Names into numerical IP Addresses. It is widely known as the 'Phonebook of the Internet' (Port 53).
DHCP (Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol) automatically assigns IP addresses and other communication parameters to devices connected to a network.
Telnet is an early network protocol used for Remote Login (Port 23), but it is considered highly insecure as it transmits all data in unencrypted plain text.
The TCP/IP suite was developed in the 1970s by Vint Cerf and Bob Kahn, who are universally recognized as the 'Fathers of the Internet'.
